order.why: Ask for hearing, sight and enduring joy.
shortened: Enlighten my eyes and make my ears hearing that I may hearken to the melody of the Kingdom and seek eternal joy and delight.

order.why: Pray for opened doors and even roads.
Join illumination with strengthened capacity.
Gather speech, hearing and sight in every condition.
shortened: May thy tongue become eloquent in the mention and praise of God, and thine ear attentive to the divine call. May thine eyes be opened to the most great signs, and mayest thou become intimate with the mysteries of the Self-Sufficing Lord.
And in all conditions mayest thou ever soar to the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Seek awareness of heart and a refuge.
Turn toward assistance.
Keep the counsel to supplicate day and night.
shortened: God has chosen you. This crown He has placed upon your head. This eternal life has been given you. Turn day and night to the Kingdome of Abha. Supplicate for boundless favors from that Kingdom.'

order.why: Pray as one hungry at the heavenly table.
Offer grace around an actual table.
Ask for a share in enduring bounty.
shortened: May we receive abundant portion from the Forgiving Lord in this age of light, may we enter the divine Kingdom, may we seek eternal grace and find everlasting bounty.

order.why: Retain the petition for success in eternal life.
shortened: We beseech God to aid thee and grant thee success and ordain for thee that which is the cause of eternal life and everlasting existence.

order.why: Connect the ultimate goal with steadfastness.
Hold contemplation and attachment to the Beloved together.
Seek what endures through trust.
Calls for the virtues and enduring life of the Kingdom.
Fix attention on the everlasting Beauty.
shortened: Be not grieved by the world and its hardships, for it was and is transient. Fix thy gaze upon the everlasting Beauty and that which hath been ordained for thee in the Kingdom.

order.why: Keep the assurance of walking in divine good-pleasure.
Attend to the station sought by the sincere.
Retain the aspiration to glory in unity.
shortened: But those who found freedom sought release from kingship - they saw the throne as a tight fetter and considered the diadem a painful torment. They found the crown to be illness itself. Therefore they sought an eternal kingdom and yearned for everlasting sovereignty. They pursued the glory of the realm of unity and desired greatness in the heavenly world. They considered servitude at the threshold to be crown and tiara, and bondage at the gate to be sovereignty over both worlds.

order.why: Keep the counsel to lofty aspiration.
shortened: O thou maidservant! Have great magnanimity, so that thou mayest be favored in the Threshold of the Almighty. Have lofty aspirations so that thou mayest attain, in the Kingdom of God, to Eternal Life.

order.why: Set physical smallness beside spiritual greatness.
Keep both present recognition and future recompense in view.
shortened: I swear by the Sun of the horizon of inner meanings that God has and will have paradises beyond compare. But in this first life, what is meant by paradise is His good-pleasure and entry into His Cause. And after the believers ascend from this world, they enter incomparable paradises and partake of boundless blessings, which are the fruits of their deeds in this world.

order.why: Explore recognition, memory and love after death.
shortened: And know thou for a certainty, that in the divine worlds, the spiritual beloved ones (believers) will recognize each other, and will seek union (with each other), but a spiritual union. Likewise, a love that one may have entertained for any one will not be forgotten in the world of the Kingdom. Likewise, thou wilt not forget (there) the life that thou hast had in the material world.

order.why: Bring the relation between worlds into reciprocal prayer.
shortened: In the next world, man will find himself freed from many of the disabilities under which he now suffers. Those who have passed on through death, have a sphere of their own. It is not removed from ours; their work--the work of the Kingdom--is ours; but it is sanctified from what we call 'time and place.'
Those who have ascended have different attributes from those who are still on earth, yet there is no real separation.
"In prayer there is a mingling of station, a mingling of condition. Pray for them as they pray for you!

order.why: Seek an intimacy without parting.
Keep friendship among the requisites of the eternal world.
shortened: In the eternal world, then, which is the world of divine unity and heavenly oneness, friendship and spiritual intimacy are naturally among the essential requisites of that sanctified world....

order.why: Let a present gathering anticipate enduring fellowship.
Read the hope of union without sorrow or separation.
shortened: Particularly to one Theosophist who expressed great joy at attaining the blessed presence, He said: "I hope our joy will be eternal, that we shall be together in all the divine worlds, that we shall find shelter under the protection of Baha'u'llah. There is union there that knows no separation, a day that has no night following it, joy that knows no sorrow, life that finds no death.

order.why: Imagine a shared meal beyond parting.
Connect present food with hoped-for divine sustenance.
Let bodily distance coexist with loving remembrance.
Follow companionship into the garden of reunion.
shortened: And so will ye nestle together hereafter, in the rose-garden of the All-Merciful in the Abha Kingdom, upon the branches of the divine Lote-Tree. For ye are the birds of the meadow of guidance and the nightingales of the bower of bounty.

order.why: Pray for family harmony beneath the Tree of Life.
Extend that hope to sons and daughter.
Receive children as future fruit-bearing trees.
shortened: Those children will, God willing, become the children of the Kingdom and, beneath the protecting shadow of the favors of the Ancient Beauty - may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones - will become fruit-bearing trees and flowers and sweet herbs in the Abha Paradise.

order.why: Join heavenly inheritance with the need for nurture.
Hear consolation addressed to a bereaved parent.
shortened: For thy beloved child has hastened to the embrace of the heavenly Father and has turned his face to the Kingdom of the All-Merciful, and the Lord, the Self-Subsisting has shown him the utmost tenderness and care.

order.why: Keep the particular promise concerning a son.
shortened: I Myself shall atone for the loss of her son -- a son who now dwelleth within the tabernacle of My majesty and glory, and whose face beameth with a light that envelopeth with its radiance the Maids of Heaven in their celestial chambers, and beyond them the inmates of My Paradise, and the denizens of the Cities of Holiness.

order.why: Let grief coexist with the image of a rekindled lamp.
Hear the assurance of a companion in divine worlds.
Remember a parent through promised spiritual life.
Preserve the quoted father’s gratitude.
shortened: That pure soul calls out from the realm of the Kingdom: "O blessed and beloved son! A hundred praises that you have made me content and honored and exalted.

order.why: Link a child’s conduct with a parent’s joy.
Read the womb analogy within the reported exchange about recognition.
Attend to a departure marked by hope and humility.
Consider the completion of spiritual life.
shortened: When he hasteneth from this world to the world of the Kingdom and maketh his way to the divine realm, then his spiritual life will attain completion.

order.why: Listen to the departed soul as a singing bird.
Hear the quoted wish that others knew of forgiveness.
shortened: Today in the horizon of the Abha Kingdom he shines like the morning star with utmost brilliance and cries out "Would that my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me and placed me among the honored ones!"

order.why: Retain the tribute expressed as spiritual sovereignty.
shortened: Today in the realm of the Kingdom he sits upon the throne of might wearing a crown of divine gifts and exercises spiritual sovereignty.

order.why: Remember the departed through the shining pearl.
Keep the joy attributed to one who has ascended.
shortened: He hath soared with the spirit, and We are now in a garden of delight.
He who hath soared to the Supreme Horizon remaineth beneath the shadow of My Hidden Name and My Resplendent Being. He is in joy and gladness.

order.why: Gather the imagery of attainment and reunion.
shortened: I bear witness that thou didst quaff from the wellspring of paradise and wert intoxicated with the choice wine proffered in the most sublime chalice, that thou didst attain unto the presence of the Most High, sought the shelter of His unsurpassing mercy, gained admittance into the Abha Kingdom, ascended unto the highest heaven, rose to the loftiest station, entered within the heavenly abode, reposed in the gardens of delight, hearkened to the melodies of the birds of holiness singing upon the blessed Tree, and wert blest with the gift of reunion and granted life everlasting.

order.why: Read angelic company through acquired heavenly attributes.
Pray for those who have taken flight.
shortened: They have become weary of the earthly world and seek the pure realm, the luminous kingdom.
O Kind God! They have been freed from this world and have taken flight to Your realm.

order.why: Join prayers for pardon with longing for reunion.
Keep the brief prayer for forgiveness and presence.
Pray that a folded wing may soar.
Connect truthful speech with later reunion.
shortened: Exalt their stations in the realm of names, and endow them with truthful tongues among the dwellers of creation. Suffer them to gain admission, after their ascension, into the heaven of reunion with the Exalted Friend.

order.why: Ask for entry into the garden of immortality.
shortened: Assist him, then, suffer him to enter the garden of immortality, and honor him with the privilege of witnessing and meeting Thee.

order.why: Join present tranquility with hope at ascension.
shortened: Suffer us to be wholly freed from this nether life, and cause us to be blessed with the bountiful gifts of the Kingdom.
Give peace to hearts and grant tranquility to souls so that when we ascend to the Kingdom we may attain Your presence and be joyous and glad in the Supreme Concourse.

order.why: Keep the hope of attainment beyond a missed earthly meeting.
Read the letter of liberation within its promise.
shortened: If thou openest the eye of thy soul and gazest upon the Kingdom of the Best-Beloved, thou wilt observe that this is a letter of liberation whereby thou shalt gain admittance to the divine Kingdom, and when thou takest flight from this dusty realm of darkness to the luminous world, thou shalt hasten to the private chamber of the Truth.

order.why: Acknowledge bestowals not yet apparent.
Keep the demanding address to Badi‘ in its own context.
shortened: Sacrifice this earthly frame for the Celestial Beloved and offer this contingent temple as an oblation to the Beloved of the realms beyond, that thou mayest witness a goodly life and an eternal existence in the Most Glorious Kingdom and observe the manifest signs.

order.why: Retain the testimony to a particular journey and attainment.
Follow the freed nightingale into its song.
Read entrance into the Kingdom as freedom from fear of death.
shortened: Those souls who enter God's Kingdom, according to Christ's words, do not die. So enter God's Kingdom so you will not fear death.

order.why: Keep the parallel reported counsel.
Return to a prison described as paradise.
Bring the fruit of fellowship into this narrow world.
shortened: Turn thy face toward the Abha Kingdom, seek to grasp the hem of His grandeur, find thy dwelling and shelter beneath the Sadratu'l-Muntaha, and partake of the fruit of the tree of fellowship, that thou mayest live in perfect contentment in this narrow mortal world and, after thy spirit's ascension, attain unto life everlasting in the eternal realm.

order.why: Recognize affinity in a present gathering.
shortened: That world is the Kingdom of complete attraction and affinity. It is the Kingdom of the One Divine Spirit, the Kingdom of God. Therefore, the affinity and love manifest in this meeting, the divine susceptibilities witnessed here are not of this world but of the world of the Kingdom.

order.why: Pray for a heavenly assembly on earth.
shortened: May the outpourings of the Holy Spirit encompass all and may an assembly of the denizens of the Kingdom be formed in this earthly realm.

order.why: Read a gathering through its orientation.
shortened: All gatherings are of the material world but praise be to God this assembly is of the divine realm. All are confined to the natural world but praise be to God you are oriented toward the divine Kingdom.

order.why: Hear the hope addressed to two named friends.
Invite others to the same table.
Keep ship, covenant and shore together.
Look for illumination within mortal existence.
shortened: I wish you to live in the world of the Spirit--to see the Divine Reality in everything,--to behold the illumination of the world of the Kingdom beyond and within the gloomy mask of this mortal existence. For the world of the Kingdom is a world of Lights, a world of happiness, a world of accomplishment, the real and eternal world.

order.why: Connect turning toward the Kingdom with service to humanity.
shortened: But when their heart is turned toward the Kingdom of God and their happiness comes from the bounties of the highest horizon, they become free from every sorrow. They attach their heart to the divine world, become the confidant of the human world, and promote the signs and mysteries of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Read heavenly power through renewed hope and strength.
shortened: Because the grace of the Kingdom of ABHA makes the weak to become strong, the poor to become wealthy; the confused one to become assured, and renders happiness to the grieved soul. It makes the disappointed soul to become hopeful, and a deprived man to become initiated. This is heavenly power.

order.why: Join consolation with divine characteristics.
shortened: This is the Cause of happiness! This is the means of consolation! The Glory of man is through the Love of God, entrance into his Kingdom and being imbued with his divine characteristics.

order.why: Follow illumination toward regeneration.
shortened: When the people live in the realm of light, then their hearts will be illumined; then their spirits will be rejoiced with the divine Glad -Tidings, then their minds will become the receptacles of the Holy Spirit; then they shall be regenerated; then they shall enter in the Kingdom of Abha.

order.why: Consider advancement and retreat through light and darkness.
Preserve the reported wording about compulsion.
Keep the supplied bracket and the question of creation’s purpose.
Let tranquility become the capacity to stir others.
Gather the claims about human nature’s sublimity.
shortened: This is the illumination of the world of humanity! This is the eternal life! This is the sublimity of human nature. This is heavenly glory! This is the radiant crown of the Kingdom of Abha!

order.why: Keep the concentrated affirmation of enduring life.
shortened: This is the eternal glory. This is the eternal life. This is the entrance into the Kingdom of God, the dominion which will last forever.

order.why: Retain the question about gaining happiness.
Hear the brief assurance of its endurance.
Ground joy and hope in bounty.
shortened: The denizens of the Kingdom derive their joy from the bounties of God and set their hopes on His infinite grace. They exult in the outpourings of divine bounty and are gladdened by the favours of the Lord of Hosts.

order.why: Keep the rejoicing of the sincere.
shortened: The sincere ones are in utmost joy and jubilation and in the highest paradise with an All-Forgiving God.

order.why: Imagine joy at what remains unknown.
shortened: The truth I say unto you! If ye were aware of what God hath destined for you in the kingdom of His glory, verily ye would rejoice exceedingly and soar with the wings of joy unto the heights of happiness, crying with the most loud voice: "Blessings and happiness from this great attainment and evident bounty."

order.why: Hear the overwhelming attraction of the opened Kingdom.
Follow love’s fire toward shining in the world beyond.
shortened: And we beseech from His abundant grace and glorious generosity that you might become so intoxicated with the wine of the love of God that you set fire to the hearts of all contingent beings, cast flames into the reality of existence, raise up commotion in earth and heaven, bring the sea of the world into waves, soar to the heights of the supreme Kingdom, and when you hasten to the Abha Kingdom your face will shine bright, your eyes will open clear, you will become the manifestation of endless favors and the dawning-place of the levels of light.

order.why: Let the open doors lead toward composure and peace.
shortened: Thank thou God that the doors of the Kingdom are opened and the way of the Truth become manifest and evident.

Therefore, enter thou completely into this divine Kingdom; that is, acquire heavenly bliss and beatitude and turn thy face to the Luminous Realm, so that the hurtful powers may be dispersed at once, eternal felicity, composure and tranquility become realized, the heart find glad-tidings, the soul, peace, and even the body, grace and beauty.

order.why: Consider bewilderment at divine attributes.
Give thanks for true vision.
shortened: Give thanks to God that thou hast attained true vision and in the ancient Kingdom hast beheld the beauty of that cherished Beloved.

order.why: Keep the recollection of traversing light.
Preserve the recognition of received bestowals.
shortened: Since you belong to this class of souls, therefore you have realized the Kingdom of God and have partaken of the bestowals of the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Connect comprehension with entering the light.
Name the reality of favor through salvation.
Let radiance be visible in faces.
Receive the assurance of belonging.
shortened: Ye are counted among the people of the immortal Kingdom. Ye must, through the assistance of the Lord of Names, sanctify and purify yourselves from unpleasing conditions and selfish limitations.

order.why: Imagine persons as enduring letters.
shortened: Such souls are accounted as letters of God's Book and abide eternally in the immortal Kingdom, enduring as God endureth.

order.why: Keep the friends’ crown and throne within its spiritual meaning.
shortened: O servant of Baha! Praise be to God that a crown from the glorious Kingdom rests upon the heads of the friends, and the eternal throne of sovereignty in that world is the felicity of the friends.

order.why: Give thanks for life in an age of spring.
Rejoice in the opened doors.
Follow souls taking wing.
Hear the announcement of the opened Kingdom.
Read the language of conquest through hearts and spirits.
shortened: O thou who art waiting for the Appearance of the Kingdom!

Glad-tidings be unto thee, for the Kingdom of God hath raised its tent and tabernacle upon the apex of the world, the standard of the Kingdom is hoisted, the call of the Kingdom is sent forth and the hosts of the Kingdom have appeared.

Therefore, there are many fortresses and castles of hearts which are conquered and many regions of spirits which are subdued. The lights of the Kingdom have shone forth from the horizon of the East and the West.

order.why: Preserve the response to a seeker’s wish.
shortened: O thou who art looking for the Kingdom of God!

Thy letter was considered. Glad tidings be unto thee for thy supreme wish became manifest in the assemblage of the world. The spacious Kingdom was newly adorned, and like unto paradise, manifested beautiful scenes.

order.why: Retain the personal recognition of attraction.
Give thanks for a youth’s wayfaring.
shortened: O spiritual youth! I have chanted verses of thanksgiving to God for what He has bestowed upon you from His grace and mercy, and for making you a wayfarer on the path of the Kingdom, receiving the favors of your loving Lord.

order.why: Join unity, guidance and the real Kingdom.
Keep the brief assurance of presence.
Read entry through pardon and forgiveness.
Let a vision of the Kingdom change conduct after bereavement.
shortened: O true servant of the Abha Beauty! After the ascension of the Blessed Beauty, may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones, holy souls forgot this world and saw themselves in the Abha Kingdom, and conducted themselves accordingly.

Their joy is the melody of the birds that rises in the rose garden of Abha, and their desire is the manifestation of the light and flame of Sinai that sheds its radiance from the hidden realm of the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Keep another life and song amid ruined buildings.
shortened: Certainly this monastery has been destroyed several times already and rebuilt twice, but God's loved ones have another mystery and another song. Their world is another world, their life another life, their air another air.

order.why: Close the linked readings with shared work in both worlds.
Bring the supplied fragment back to a place of worship.
Explore the distinct terminology of the realm of similitudes.
Keep the Bab’s supplied account of worlds and its omission.
Retain mediation and inner conditions in the attributed letter.
Consider John of the Cross’s degrees of love in their own tradition.
Keep the supplied Thomas fragment and its unseen Kingdom.
Let the mustard seed open the comparison to hidden growth.
Close with preparation in present life.

questions: What changes when the Kingdom is understood as a spiritual reality rather than a location, and what questions remain difficult to express?
How do the images of birth, a magnet, food, light, and a garden illuminate different aspects of spiritual life?
How can detachment and attention to an eternal world deepen care for the people and responsibilities immediately around us?
What do the readings on grief, memory, recognition, and enduring friendship contribute to thinking about relationships across death?
How do Matthew’s seed and leaven and Paul’s account of peace and joy help you read this compilation, and where do their particular Christian settings matter?
Which qualities or practices might make the Kingdom perceptible in a family, gathering, or community, and how could those qualities be cultivated?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 13:31–33 · Mustard seed and leaven
references.note: Read the supplied mustard-seed passage together with the next parable of leaven. Both portray the Kingdom through a small or hidden beginning whose effects spread. Compare these images of growth with the compilation’s gardens, spiritual birth, and preparation in this life, without assuming that every image gives the same account of the Kingdom.

references.label: 2 · Romans 14:17–19 · Righteousness, peace, and joy
references.note: Paul describes the Kingdom through righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit, connecting service to Christ with building one another up. Read this practical emphasis alongside the compilation’s fellowship, moral qualities, and work for the Kingdom on earth, while preserving the passage’s specifically Christian orientation.

subjects.displayTitle: Unity in diversity: the beauty and work of belonging
subjects.introduction: Were every part of a body an eye, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes, it would have no beauty and no life; it is eye, ear and hand, each keeping its own office, that let one spirit move the whole. Unity in diversity means not the flattening of difference but its gathering, as varied notes make a chord and many-coloured flowers make a garden lovelier than any single hue. The hard part is telling which differences enrich and which destroy. Innate variety of temperament, capacity and culture is a gift; antagonism bred of ignorance and prejudice tears families and nations apart and has to be unlearned. So the teaching asks for disciplines: consulting before acting, weighing another’s view before pressing one’s own, teaching without airs of superiority, the strong bearing with the weak, and the courtesy that lets people of different faiths and races trade and dine together. Paul’s picture of necessary members who suffer and rejoice as one [1], and the Qur’an’s word that peoples were made distinct so that they might know one another [2], sharpen the question of what belonging requires. Beyond lies the work of race unity, the freedom of diverse thought and belief, and the oneness of humanity on which a world society must rest.
subjects.arc: Open with interdependence and the value of difference; distinguish unity from coercion and destructive conflict; examine the disciplines of understanding, racial equality and religious fellowship; widen toward shared institutions, cultural identity and complementary action.

order.why: Let different musical notes make the image audible.
Open with the distinct organs contributing to one body.
shortened: Observe the human body, its limbs, its members, the eye, the ear, the organs of smell, of taste, the hands, the fingernails. Notwithstanding the differences among all these parts, each one within the limitations of its own being participateth in a coherent whole.

order.why: Ground humane association in common creation.
shortened: The All Mighty hath created all people from the same stock, all humanity belongs to the same grade or station: thou shouldst never see differences in the creation of God One should treat all created things with humanity; one should associate and consort with all people with the utmost love and concord, which is born of the All Merciful.

order.why: Distinguish differences of capacity from equality as human beings.
Distinguish inner conviction from imposed uniformity.
Ask directly which differences enrich and which destroy.
shortened: In answer we say that differences are of two kinds. One is the cause of annihilation and is like the antipathy existing among warring nations and conflicting tribes who seek each other's destruction, uprooting one another's families, depriving one another of rest and comfort and unleashing carnage. The other kind which is a token of diversity is the essence of perfection and the cause of the appearance of the bestowals of the Most Glorious Lord.

order.why: Join the garden’s diversity with a unifying source.
shortened: Consider the flowers of a garden: though differing in kind, colour, form and shape, yet, inasmuch as they are refreshed by the waters of one spring, revived by the breath of one wind, invigorated by the rays of one sun, this diversity increases their charm, and adds unto their beauty. Thus when that unifying force, the penetrating influence of the Word of God, takes effect, the difference of customs, manners, habits, ideas, opinions and dispositions embellishes the world of humanity, and this is praiseworthy.

order.why: Keep the Races Congress account of customs and dispositions.
shortened: Observe the flowers of the gardens: though they differ in kind, vary in color, and are diverse in form and shape, yet, since they drink of one water, grow by one breeze, and are nurtured by the heat and light of one sun, that diversity and difference become the cause of increasing the beauty and splendor of each. Likewise, when the unifying agency---the penetrating power of the Word of God---is attained, these differences of customs, manners, habits, thoughts, opinions, and dispositions become the adornment of the world of humanity.

order.why: Give each member its own indispensable office.
shortened: We know very well that such temple is composed of many members which differ greatly in shape, form, action and office, and when these different members act in harmony with each other and have the real perfect affinity and attraction among them, they form together that temple which will be thoroughly ready to receive the spirit--although so various and different. We cannot say that one member is preferred to another, or is of greater importance in the formation of the temple. No, we cannot say that, for each member has its own office and by the action of all in harmony and unison, a perfect result is produced.

order.why: Ground the inquiry in mutual helpfulness.
shortened: For the world of humanity, nay, rather, all the infinite beings exist by this law of mutual action and helpfulness. Should this law of joint interchange of forces be removed from the arena of life, the existence would be entirely destroyed.

order.why: Retain individuality within the image of an ocean.
shortened: Taking the material ocean as an illustration, 'Abduil-Baha said, The atoms composing an ocean are, in appearance the ocean, but the identity of the atoms remains. So it is with our individuality in the ocean of life, it remains.

order.why: Read essential differences as sources of splendor.
Distinguish innate variety from learned antagonism.
shortened: There are two kinds of differences: one kind is essential and innate differences, which do not prevent the manifestation of general unity and fellowship, but rather support it - like the different colors and types of flowers in a garden that contribute to its increased beauty and adornment, or like the different members of the human body which all assist one another and cause the appearance and manifestation of each other's perfections.

The other kind consists of accidental differences which, due to lack of education, become the source of ignorance and cruelty, and the cause of oppression, enmity, hatred and warfare between the nations of the world.

order.why: Give each person an individual fragrance and color.
shortened: Therefore, although we are of different individualities, different in ideas and of various fragrances, let us strive like flowers of the same divine garden to live together in harmony. Even though each soul has its own individual perfume and color, all are reflecting the same light, all contributing fragrance to the same breeze which blows through the garden, all continuing to grow in complete harmony and accord. Become as waves of one sea, trees of one forest, growing in the utmost love, agreement and unity.

order.why: Welcome differing personalities.
Consider variety through food and different degrees.
Read the whole through diverse members and occupations.
Let specialized work coexist without condemnation.
Explore mutual dependence in the source’s account of living kingdoms.
Hold shared natural processes beside significant distinctions.
shortened: All of them pass through the process of composition and decomposition; this is a natural law to which all are subject. This law is ruling throughout creation and constitutes a bond of connection among created things. But at the same time there are certain distinguishing features between these objects. For instance, between the mineral and vegetable, the vegetable and animal, the animal and human, points of distinction exist which are unmistakable and significant.

order.why: Read connection as peace in the world of phenomena.
Imagine a part expressing the potential of a whole.
Consider the significance of pairing at different scales.
Keep the Bab’s account of pairs in its revealed terminology.
Read a single creative word through varied effects.
Read the sun’s bounty as given without favoritism.
Join one ocean and light with manifold waves and beings.
Distinguish unity of essence from variety of expression.
shortened: When he says, "Ye are all the leaves of one branch," he infers the inherent differences between men, differences like unto the leaves. Nature manifests in various forms, but the basic element is the same. There is unity of essence and variety of expression.

order.why: Read one spirit through differentiated parts.
Return to harmony preparing the human temple.
shortened: The Kingdom of God is also likened unto the temple of man. We know very well that such temple is composed of many members which differ greatly in shape, form, action and office, and when these different members act in harmony with each other and have the real perfect affinity and attraction among them, they form together that temple which will be thoroughly ready to receive the Spirit - although so various and different.

order.why: Explore the body analogy’s account of a collective power.
shortened: If the body of man merely consisted of eyes, or head, or ears, it would have no beauty. The oneness of the spirit has given such a unity to these organs that the differences are as ornaments for the body.
Likewise in this world of existence there must appear or manifest a collective aspect like unto the spirit (in man) with a power to dominate the different elements of the body of humanity.
As the spirit of man unites and harmonizes the different organs of the body, so the Word of God shall unite the differ nations of the world.

order.why: Follow many radii toward one center.
Compare bouquet, elements, body and flowing water.
shortened: The flowers are of different form, color and odor; each is individual in its essence; yet they form a beautiful whole. Another kind of gathering is like a flock of birds- they are each of different intention. Then there is the gathering of the elements, which are united and form a new substance. Also, the various parts of the body, which unite to form a being. There are the drops which meet and flow together into one, and these flowing on form a river which flows on and then we have the sea and the ocean.

order.why: Hear two readers challenged to relinquish mutual accusation.
Preserve the acceptance of different degrees of understanding.
Begin teaching without claims of superiority.
Consider the practical demands of spiritual chemistry.
Consider another person’s view before insisting on one’s own.
shortened: Man should weigh his opinions with the utmost serenity, calmness and composure. Before expressing his own views he should carefully consider the views already advanced by others. If he finds that a previously expressed opinion is more true and worthy, he should accept it immediately and not willfully hold to an opinion of his own. By this excellent method he endeavors to arrive at unity and truth. Opposition and division are deplorable.

order.why: Make consultation a practice of careful inquiry.
shortened: For example, should a person desire to undertake a work, if he consults about it with a number of his brethren, undoubtedly, through deliberation, careful discussion and investigation, the acceptable course will become clear and the real situation manifest and evident.
To go a step further: if the inhabitants of a village consult together about their own affairs, it is certain that the path of Right will be disclosed to them.

order.why: Attend to different listeners through different subjects.
Acknowledge the administrative difficulty of diverse understandings.
shortened: The Cause has become very great. Many souls are entering it--souls with different mentalities and degrees of understanding. Complex difficulties constantly rise before us. The administration of the Cause has become most difficult. Conflicting thought and theories attack the Cause from every side. Now consider to what extent the believers in God must become firm and soul-sacrificing. Every one of the friends must become the essence of essences; each one must become a brilliant lamp.

People all around the world are entering the Cause; people of various tribes and nations and religions and sects. It is most difficult to administer to such heterogeneous elements. Wisdom and Divine insight are necessary.

order.why: Read the argument for a universal perceptive power.
Keep the warning about asking God to support one’s opinion.
shortened: For instance, some difference of opinion arises between two believers in God. Each expects the Lord to support his view of the question.
Discord and disagreement are impossible among those who adhere to the Manifestation and sever themselves from human opinion.'

order.why: Ask what is missed by attachment to names.
Let the grapes expose a misunderstanding of words.
Consider a shared language alongside a person’s own.
Bring beliefs into conversation with science.
Invite people of differing religions to inquire of one another.
shortened: A bright century dawns, the ultimate result will be Unity. The Christian may inquire from the Jew as to the foundation of Judaism,-of the Zoroastrian concerning the moralization of man. This is idealism and progress.

order.why: Give that encounter a home in education.
Open Green Acre to leaders of different thought.
Keep the reported appreciation of free inquiry in its setting.
shortened: The Theosophists are very dear to me, for they have abandoned all prejudice. They do not abide in the confines of dogma, but are seeking truth in a spirit of freedom. All the religions of the world are submerged in prejudice.

order.why: Recognize service under a different flag.
shortened: God and His servants are also pleased with those souls who are serving under a different flag and in a different camp to actualize these principles of humanity."

order.why: Join receptive speech with praiseworthy conduct.
shortened: The friends of Truth must speak such words as will immediately make beings receptive, and adorn themselves with goodly deeds, pleasing character, and praiseworthy conduct which are the cause and means of the world's tranquility and the order of nations.

order.why: Practice dignified and composed association.
shortened: Unity and concord are beloved today and have ever been. Associate with all the peoples of the world with the utmost spirit, fragrance, dignity and composure, that your goodly character may spread its fragrance among them.

order.why: Ask the strong to assist the weak with forbearance.
shortened: Be ye united and in accord in the Cause of God. The strong must assist the weak with the utmost kindliness and forbearance, that all may act according to the goodly deeds which have been revealed in the divine Tablets, and may become purified and sanctified from selfish desires and vain imaginings.

order.why: Let humility give unity influence.
Remove rancor while cultivating fidelity.
shortened: By God's life! We love to see each one of you sanctified from rancor and hatred, and adorned with love and fidelity. We beseech God to send down upon you, from the heaven of grace and bounty, a mercy from His presence and a blessing from His own Self.

order.why: Conquer hearts through wisdom and utterance.
Consider the effect of discordant public speech.
shortened: Unity in one station is unity in speech, and this is highly essential. Consider, for example, if two of God's loved ones were to enter a land and speak differently about a matter, this would cause dissension, and they themselves and others would be deprived of the blessing of unity which hath been revealed from the Pen of the Lord of all creation.

order.why: Hear grief at discord among the friends.
shortened: Convey loving greetings from this servant to the loved ones of God and say that the Manifestation of Truth is for love, unity, oneness, agreement, sincerity and fairness.
Surely the friends of God will not be content that while I hope for affection and unity, I see signs of trouble and discord. I become very saddened and grieved.

order.why: Read the garden in the Howard University address.
Connect racial equality with divine possibilities.
shortened: God maketh no distinction between the white and the black. If the hearts are pure both are acceptable unto Him. God is no respecter of persons on account of either color or race. All colors are acceptable to Him, be they white, black, or yellow. Inasmuch as all were created in the image of God, we must bring ourselves to realize that all embody divine possibilities. If you go into a garden and find all the flowers alike in form, species and color, the effect is wearisome to the eye. The garden is more beautiful when the flowers are many-colored and different; the variety lends charm and adornment.

order.why: Let each color contribute to a shared beauty.
shortened: He has declared that difference of race and color is like the variegated beauty of flowers in a garden. If you enter a garden, you will see yellow, white, blue, red flowers in profusion and beauty -- each radiant within itself and although different from the others, lending its own charm to them. Racial difference in the human kingdom is similar. If all the flowers in a garden were of the same color, the effect would be monotonous and wearying to the eye.

order.why: Bring the image into an interracial gathering.
shortened: I am very happy that white and black are together. This is the cause of my happiness, for you all are the servants of one God and, therefore, brothers, sisters, mothers and fathers. In the sight of God there is no distinction between whites and blacks; all are as one. Anyone whose heart is pure is dear to God -- whether white or black, red or yellow.

Associate with each other, think of each other, and be like a rose garden. Anyone who goes into a rose garden will see various roses, white, pink, yellow, red, all growing together and replete with adornment. Each one accentuates the beauty of the other.

order.why: Keep the historical explanation of the flower image attributed.
Retain the concise affirmation of equal acceptance.
Join racial fellowship with service and dignity.
shortened: I hope that ye may cause that downtrodden race to become glorious, and to be joined with the white race, to serve the world of man with the utmost sincerity, faithfulness, love, and purity.

order.why: Preserve the call for just and mutual consideration and its omission.
Read variety as needed for beauty.
Keep the comparison with animals in its source setting.
Retain the reported contrast of animal associations.
Retain the reported rejection of class and denominational hostility.
Welcome all through the light of oneness.
Look beyond outward differences.
Refuse distinctions of homeland and race as barriers.
shortened: Praise be to God that the hearts of the friends are united and in agreement, whether one is from the East or West, South or North, whether German or French, Japanese or American, white or black, red or yellow or brown. Differences of color, homeland and race have no significance in the Baha'i Cause. Rather, the Baha'i unity prevails over all and eliminates all these illusions.

order.why: Attend to justice wherever its light appears.
Connect freedom from prejudice with human interests.
Read prejudice through the branches of one tree.
shortened: He broke the chains of religious prejudice, racial bigotry, patriotic fanaticism, and political animosity, and compared the world of humanity to a tree and all peoples to its branches, leaves, blossoms, and fruits.

order.why: Meet the person beyond national labels.
shortened: Do not say, he is an Italian, or a Frenchman, or an American, or an Englishman, remember only that he is a son of God, a servant of the Most High, a man! All are men! Forget nationalities; all are equal in the sight of God!

order.why: Keep the parallel counsel about national distinctions.
shortened: Never say this one is English, that one German, this French, that Italian - do not utter these distinctions. You are all servants and handmaids of God, peace be upon you.

order.why: Hold women and men together in humanity’s development.
Keep the source’s argument about relative value.
Read the reported complementary-spheres language in its historical setting.
Keep the reported claim about intermarriage attributed.
Consider marriages joining distant families.
Receive marriage through prosperity and shared bounty.
See diversity present at a wedding.
Seek truth and light beyond their names and locations.
shortened: Likewise, the divine religions of the holy Manifestations of God are in reality one, though in name and nomenclature they differ. Man must be a lover of the light, no matter from what dayspring it may appear. He must be a lover of the rose, no matter in what soil it may be growing. He must be a seeker of the truth, no matter from what source it come.

order.why: Read religions as collective centers.
shortened: The divine religions are collective centers in which diverse standpoints may meet, agree and unify. They accomplish oneness of native lands, races and policies. For instance, Christ united various nations, brought peace to warring peoples and established the oneness of humankind.

order.why: Examine love of God as a power of reconciliation.
shortened: We stand therefore in need of a universal power which can prevail over the thoughts, opinions and sentiments of all, which can annul these divisions and bring all souls under the sway of the principle of the oneness of humanity. And it is clear and evident that the greatest power in the human world is the love of God. It gathers diverse peoples under the shade of the tabernacle of oneness and fosters the greatest love and fellowship among hostile and contending peoples and nations.

order.why: Connect prophetic purpose with unity and its cost.
Distinguish the effects of love’s fire and enmity’s flame.
shortened: The brightness of the fire of your love will no doubt fuse and unify the contending peoples and kindreds of the earth, whilst the fierceness of the flame of enmity and hatred cannot but result in strife and ruin.

order.why: Read the true balance through love.
Join unity’s recognition with good conduct.
shortened: Such nearness cannot be attained except through goodly deeds and praiseworthy conduct. Deeds and their acceptance are, in the first instance and highest station, dependent upon the divine unity. Praise be to God that the favored community is adorned with the crown of recognition and the ornament of unity, and at all times utters and remembers the blessed words "There is none other God but God."

order.why: Keep unity as a support of the Cause.
shortened: O My Name, the All-Bountiful! All the loved ones of God must at all times fix their gaze upon this utterance of the All-Merciful which, like unto the sun, hath shone forth from the horizon of the heaven of God's Holy Tablet: "We have made unity the support for the pavilions of My Cause and the cord for the tabernacle of My glory. Hold fast unto it, O My servants, then act according to that which God hath revealed in His wondrous Tablet."

order.why: Retain the specified limits within the call to unity.
shortened: The Supreme Pen proclaims: O friends of Truth! The purpose of bearing these successive afflictions and consecutive trials is that souls assured in God should walk together in perfect unity, such that all difference, duality and otherness might be effaced from their midst, save in those special limitations that have been sent down in the divine Books.

order.why: Read common life with the source’s stated qualification.
shortened: Then remove ye the differences between them and gather ye together upon a single matter, such that ye may soar in a single heaven and walk upon a single earth and sit upon a single carpet and eat of a single bounty until their spirits and their light and their bodies and their forms become a single spirit and a single thing, and no separation appeareth between them save in what God hath ordained in the Book.

order.why: Extend counsel beyond those nearby.
Keep the severe contrast of response in its revealed setting.
shortened: Soon will He raise you up in truth - verily He is the Almighty, the All-Glorious.
Through unity the face of the Cause becomes illumined and the faces of those who have disbelieved in God, the Lord of the Day of Mutual Calling, are darkened.

order.why: Retain the preference for the Most Great Path.
Give truthfulness and friendship a place beneath one pavilion.
shortened: In short, the divine teachings constitute the unicolored pavilion of the oneness of the world of humanity.

The friends of God must therefore deal with the communities of the world with the utmost truthfulness and friendship without any distinction of race, so that all may embrace one another and with the utmost harmony and love may engage in the glorification of the Lord of the Kingdom.

order.why: Keep the dye-vat image beside the garden’s different colors.
shortened: All gathered at this fountain and drank from this sweet spring, taking shelter in the shade of the Divine Lote Tree and making their nests under the Tree of Paradise.

Observe what divine power and spiritual force this is that has taken all these different colored garments and dipped them in this divine vat of single color. All colors have become one color, and those multicolored garments have taken on colorlessness.

order.why: Read the particular claim about overcoming prejudice in its context.
shortened: It is impossible for these racial, religious, national and political prejudices to be eliminated except through entering under the shadow of Baha'u'llah, as is evident and clear in the East where Muslim, Jew, Zoroastrian, Christian, Brahmin and Buddhist have mixed together in utmost love and harmony to such an extent that they have become as one race. These names have been completely removed.

order.why: Keep the counsel about shared Baha’i identity in its addressed setting.
Place the reported statement about religious affiliation beside it.
Read the many-fruited tree as a particular claim of fulfillment.
shortened: A Baha'i is at the same time a Christian, a Jew, a Zoroastrian and a Mohamadan. The Baha'i Cause is like unto a tree on the branches of which you will find all manner of fruits; it is the ultimate goal to which all the paths are converging.

order.why: Retain both shared teachings and distinct principles.
Consider the reported account of a common spiritual basis.
Keep the account of fellowship across competing affiliations.
Attend to the proposed discussion of essential Christian principles.
Read wolf and lamb through reconciled peoples.
Remember the historical example of refuge and toleration.
Keep the attributed account of courtesy and association.
shortened: In the Bayan (the Book of Laws of the Bab), even more in the Kitab-i-Aqdas, it is commanded to train children and youth to utmost courtesy, for a courteous person honours his fellow-man, he cannot but be peaceable and tolerant. The positive command to courtesy and the strict prohibition of ritual impurity serve an immediate practical purpose, namely: the free association of merchants of the divers religions and races is thereby initiated and fostered, and the great goals of the Baha'i Teachings of the brotherhood of man, world unity and world peace - are brought closer to realization.

order.why: Hear the account of fellowship in Persia.
shortened: In Persia today through the teachings of Baha'u'llah you will find people of various beliefs and denominations living together in the utmost peace and agreement. The former enmities and hatred have passed away, and they exercise the utmost love toward all mankind, for they realize and know that all are the creatures and servants of one God.

order.why: Read diverse believers through family relationships.
shortened: Christians, Jews, Zoroastrians, Hindus, Buddhists and Persians all consort together with perfect love and fellowship, as if for a thousand years they had belonged to the same kindred and family; indeed, as if they were father and son, mother and daughter, sister and brother.

order.why: Retain the Universalist Church address’s particular examples.
Notice the Covenant’s role in the reported gathering.
shortened: Consider what the power of the Covenant has done! It was an impossibility for a Zoroastrian to unite with a Siyyid and a mulla with a Jew. And for these to assemble with a Christian was an absolute impossibility. But the power of the Covenant has even so gathered them that they are accounted as one spirit. Although the bodies are numerous, the spirit is one.

order.why: Read association across formerly opposed communities.
Keep the report of equity within a mixed assembly.
Hear the parallel account of brothers and sisters.
Follow national and religious variety into one gathering.
Read shared tables against former exclusion.
Attend to cooperation as an effect of teaching.
shortened: This remarkable Personage was able by these principles to establish a bond of unity among the differing sects and divergent people of Persia. Those who followed His teachings, no matter from what denomination or faction they came, were conjoined by the ties of love, until now they cooperate and live together in peace and agreement.

order.why: Preserve the account addressed at the Grand Hotel.
shortened: Today in Persia, for instance, there are many people of various races and religions who have followed the exhortations of Baha'u'llah and are living together in love and fellowship without religious, patriotic or racial prejudices -- Muslims, Jews, Christians, Buddhists, Zoroastrians and many others.

order.why: Keep the image of teachings entering humanity’s life.
Read freedom from estrangement in the reported community.
Notice faces reflecting unity in the Denver address.
shortened: Today in Persia and the Orient you will find the followers of Baha'u'llah united in the closest ties of fellowship and love. They have abandoned religious prejudices and have become as one family. When you enter their meetings, you will find Christians, Muslims, Buddhists, Zoroastrians, Jews and representatives of other beliefs present, all conjoined in a wonderful unity without a trace of bigotry or fanaticism, and the light of the oneness of the world of humanity reflected in their faces.

order.why: Connect fellowship with willingness to serve peace.
shortened: There are many wonderful teachings in the writings of Baha'u'llah which have been published in book form. They are such as will bring great blessing to the world and will be the means of establishing peace among mankind. In Persia many meetings are being held in which different religions are represented, Jewish, Christian, Mohammedan and Zoroastrian. There is harmony and friendship among them. They are at all tines ready to sacrifice their lives for one another. They serve with heart and soul in the cause of international peace.

order.why: Hear shared chanting as an expression of association.
shortened: If you go to Persia where the friends of Abha are many, you will at once realize the unifying force of God's work. They are doing their utmost to strengthen this bond of amity. There, people of different nationalities gather in one meeting and chant the divine tablets with one accord.

order.why: Retain the counsel to mention the teachings’ effects.
Keep the reported account of unity within laws and teachings.
shortened: And today we see diverse groups from different countries and of various nationalities have found sincere love and true unity within the refuge of His laws and teachings.

order.why: Read the gathering of followers beneath one tent.
Connect transformed character with enduring effects.
shortened: Moreover, these divine teachings are accompanied by a mysterious power and unmistakable confirmation, one after another - this power and confirmation being specific to the Religion of God and the Word of God. It transforms hearts, causes the improvement of the character of all, and brings about unity among peoples and parties of every land and region. It unifies diverse groups in such a way that they give their lives for one another, and raises them to such heights that their abasement is transformed into eternal glory and their effects remain permanent and lasting in all divine worlds, even in the world of dust.

order.why: Keep the account of martyrdom changing relations.
shortened: Praise be to God that the martyrdom of His loved ones in this Most Great Cause transformed rejection and denial into acceptance and recognition, such that this party now associates with all the world's parties in utmost love and fellowship.

order.why: Notice everyday coexistence in the Pilgrims Home.
shortened: Consider the influence of the Word of God that although men of totally different temperament, religion, culture and ideas live in the Pilgrims Home never do we hear even a faint whisper of ill-feeling against each other. They are welded together by the alchemy of Truth.

order.why: Retain the particular feast hosted for pilgrims of Jewish descent.
shortened: [In a feast held in 'Abdu'l-Baha's house, He remarked:] This feast belongs to the illustrious pilgrims of the Jewish descent. Through the favors of the Blessed Beauty, many diverse people have gathered in this assembly and partaken of this spiritual sustenance - Jewish, Christian or Muslim descendents, and friends from both the East and the West - each coming from a different locality arriving at this Land.

order.why: Picture varied guests seated at one dinner.
shortened: Do you remember that night in Haifa when people of many lands and nationalities were present at dinner --Americans, Persians, Europeans, persian Turks in huge sheep-skin head-gears, and European and American ladies in their wonderful hats, made part of the same meeting, which was also attended by Qayim Maqam (Governor of Haifa) and the turbaned Turkish Judge?

order.why: Ask what made their fellowship possible.
Read a present gathering as a glimpse of future fellowship.
shortened: Hearts are connected to one another, and all souls are gladdened through the grace of the Blessed Beauty. From this gathering it is clear and evident what will occur in the future, and how fellowship, unity and oneness will be achieved among the different nations, religions, peoples and warring, conflicting tribes.

order.why: Distinguish being in one meeting from being united in heart.
shortened: Today is a beautiful day. I have been longing to see such a day. I am very happy. My happiness is from the point that it is the power of God which has gathered us together, that while before we were far apart now we are together.  Were it not for the power of the Word of God such a meeting were impossible. We are all gathered together in love. While it is possible for different nations to arrange a meeting together still their hearts are not united. But such a meeting as this, of different nations united in heart, is from the power of the Word of God.

order.why: Attend to fellowship beyond ordinary shared interests.
shortened: Between us there is no patriotic, linguistic, racial, commercial nor political relation. No worldly bond nor connection of any kind exists between us that would justify such a gathering as this. The love of God has brought us together, and this is the best of means and motive. Every other bond of friendship is limited in effectiveness, but fellowship based upon the love of God is unlimited, everlasting, divine and radiant.

order.why: Read the pleasure of that shared gathering.
Keep differing customs beside spiritual attraction.
Hear another account of distance overcome by love.
shortened: Our countries are different and far from one another, and in the same way our national customs and habits are different, our languages, our opinions and thoughts are different; in every way we are very far from one another. But the influence of the word of God has gathered us, and we are here together in perfect love.

order.why: Read the meeting of East and West on common ground.
Imagine welcome despite the absence of a shared language.
Recognize a journey made for spiritual communion.
shortened: A number of persons coming from the Orient to the Occident for this purpose, this is very wonderful. You cannot find a record of it in any history of any nation.

At the utmost a person, or a number of persons, make cross the continent for sightseeing, for trade or commerce, but simply to travel for the meeting of the friends and for the sake of spiritual communion, this is very rare.

order.why: Receive affectionate remembrance across distant lands.
Let distant people become one household.
Distinguish physical proximity from spiritual affinity.
Imagine love’s fragrance passing between East and West.
shortened: God is Most Great! What a paradise has been opened in these days, and what a carpet of divine unity has been spread, such that if a servant among God's servants be in the East of the world and another servant in the West, always does the easterner inhale the holy divine fragrances from the direction of the West, and this westerner catches the sweet scents of the spirit of love from the East.

order.why: Name an opened door of international interdependence.
Consider the peace and confidence of shared beauty.
shortened: The composite beauty of humanity will be witnessed in their unity and blending. How glorious the spectacle of real unity among mankind! How conducive to peace, confidence and happiness if races and nations were united in fellowship and accord!

order.why: Give mutual exchange a practical purpose in civilization.
See children contributing across continents.
shortened: Observe how the confirmations of the Blessed Beauty have connected East and West - the children of Khurasan are contributing to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar of Chicago.

order.why: Read distant regions as a single gathering.
shortened: The power of the Abha Kingdom has established connection - East has embraced West, distant regions have drawn near, the face of the earth has taken on the character of a single gathering.

order.why: Let different names share one letter.
shortened: O friends! How wonderful it is that the blessed names of different peoples are included in one letter, for they have cast aside differences and sought unity, they have turned from estrangement to oneness. The stranger has become friend, the foreigner familiar, the distant near. Asia and America, Turk and Tajik, Europe and Africa have embraced one another, and this is through the grace of your Lord, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

order.why: Keep the friends remembered in their variety.
shortened: The friends - Turkish, Tajik, Persian and American, Muslim, Jewish, Zoroastrian and Christian - all pass before the eye of heart and soul in waves at every moment.

order.why: Notice the pleasure of remembering them together.
shortened: The purpose is to mention the handmaidens of the Merciful and remember the loved ones of God - all together is more pleasant and attractive and sweeter and more delightful, for it indicates a state of agreement and unity and oneness, that those numbered individuals have the ruling of a single person, and those many souls are manifestations of the outpourings of the One True Reality.

order.why: Hear East and West singing one melody.
Affirms that diverse waves do not prevent the sea’s unity.
Picture directions clasping hands.
shortened: What a bounty is this, and what a gift, that all points of the earth have become as a single point, and all regions have turned toward a single spot. The East has embraced the West, and the South and North have clasped hands in greeting. All have entered beneath the divine pavilion, and the Tree of Life has cast its shadow over all horizons.

order.why: Pray for estranged communities to embrace.
Join two seas and branches in a shared hope.
Give thanks beneath the common Tree.
Let many luminous bodies preserve one another.
Retain the particular claim about this cycle.
Read scattered forces being trained for service.
shortened: Whether we live in the East or in the West, the invisible Power of Baha'u'llah is unifying our scattered forces and training us for the service of His Kingdom--the kingdom of universal love and inter-racial amity.

order.why: Keep the reported hope of one family and its omission.
shortened: Then this world will become one family. There will remain no racial distinction such as French, English, American, German, Arab, Turk, Persian. They will become all one...

order.why: Receive the call to primal unity.
Consider the claim of a common country.
Question human boundaries through the created world.
Connect world citizenship with trustworthiness.
Retain the reported immigration counsel as a particular historical statement.
Keep the historical counsel to benefit all inhabitants attributed.
Question making peoples fight over rulers’ disagreements.
Hear the appeal to try care amid the threat of conflict.
shortened: It was like a barrel of gunpowder that with the least spark would explode and scorch everything in its grasp. I said to them, 'People, exert your efforts to protect humanity from this peril. You have tried all manners of politics, now come try the divine politics. If it does not have desirable results, you can quickly abandon it and return to your former ways.' Has anyone seen harm in affection? What evil is there when the people of the world learn to love and care for one another as this assemblage does?"

order.why: Keep the identification of peace as the century’s great question.
shortened: Each century has its momentous question - though there are countless issues, one issue takes on supreme importance. In the last century, the most important of issues was political freedom, and this aim spread. However, in this luminous century the greatest gift to the human world is universal peace.

order.why: Retain the reported expectation about oneness.
Let unity extend to every level of human life.
shortened: Beyond this it is obvious and observable, in the written Divine and indisputable tablets that the primary Divine Principal and goal, The Holy Will of God, is none other than the unity of all the peoples of the world, that the Oneness of the entire human race, composed of all the diverse, antagonistic and distinct ethnic groups prevails to the extent that God's Word "Unity" is embodied and characterized on all levels, so that this earthy kingdom mirrors the Heavenly Kingdom.

order.why: Join education with a common order and city.
shortened: Bend your minds and wills to the education of the peoples and kindreds of the earth, that haply the dissensions that divide it may, through the power of the Most Great Name, be blotted out from its face, and all mankind become the upholders of one Order, and the inhabitants of one City.

order.why: Carry universal love into a particular place.
Pray for illumined lives serving peace.
shortened: I hope that you may be so enlightened that you may illuminate the Horizons. I hope each one may become a lighted candle. I hope ye may become the signs of God. I hope you become heralds of the Kingdom. I hope ye may become the cause of the union of the hearts of all mankind and succeed in uniting the religions - that this dark world may become illumined and the foundation of war and dissention may be eradicated; that the standard of Universal Peace may be raised in all horizons, and table of Love be spread among all people.

order.why: Receive the hope for fellowship across religions and races.
Set aside imitation while serving humanity.
Invite Zoroastrian friends to unite familiar and stranger.
shortened: May the Zoroastrian friends, through truth-worship, friendship and honesty, adorn the gathering of the world, attain eternal life, and surpassing their ancient glory, beautify the ways of humanity and become the cause of unity and oneness between all, familiar and stranger alike.

order.why: Connect local affection with outward influence.
shortened: If the friends achieve oneness and become entirely detached from estrangement, and embrace one another, and follow the way and conduct of 'Abdu'l-Baha, in a short time that region will become fragrant with musk.

order.why: Compare unity through patriotism, war, commerce and ideals.
Keep the reported variety of collective forces.
shortened: There are many collective forces in the world of existence which bring together the scattered, which unite different ideals and give uniformity to diverse customs.

order.why: Consider the limits of externally tying people together.
shortened: To this 'Abdu'l-Baha said, "Your members may be compared to beams of different metals and you are trying to unite them as you would tie these fingers together with a string."

order.why: Read the Holy Spirit as the proposed common channel.
Distinguish situational accommodation from enduring concord.
Acknowledge divided interests and their effects.
Keep the particular analogy of Iran as a divided body.
Attend to the counsel to set aside competing aims.
shortened: However, if all parties would set aside their various aims and turn to unity and agreement, divine confirmations and heavenly assistance would surely manifest with utmost glory and beauty.

order.why: Ask what effort a professed commitment to reality demands.
Give a Spiritual Assembly responsibility for overcoming prejudice.
shortened: As for the Spiritual Assembly, I pray that God may assist them in all affairs and enable them to exalt the Word of God and promote the divine teachings, so that they may become the cause of human unity and the spread of the divine breaths, until no prejudice remains between religions, denominations and races, and all may hold fast together to the cord of God, and misunderstandings between all parties may vanish, and the human world may become a mirror of the Kingdom of God upon which spiritual lights shine.

order.why: Welcome a meeting of different denominations.
Value a church open to everyone.
Let an institution’s charity cross race and color.
Read the appeal to fraternize beyond dogmatic barriers.
Keep the friends engaged with other peoples.
Explore representation as speaking with others’ trust.
Give a gathering the purpose of peace and shared welfare.
shortened: This meeting of yours tonight is very different in character. It is a universal gathering; it is heavenly and divine in purpose because it serves the oneness of the world of humanity and promotes international peace. It is devoted to the solidarity and brotherhood of the human race, the spiritual welfare of mankind, unity of religious belief through knowledge of God and the reconciliation of religious teaching with the principles of science and reason.

order.why: Trace the effects of fellowship from family to city.
shortened: If love and agreement are manifest in a single family, that family will advance, become illumined and spiritual; but if enmity and hatred exist within it, destruction and dispersion are inevitable. This is, likewise, true of a city. If those who dwell within it manifest a spirit of accord and fellowship, it will progress steadily and human conditions become brighter, whereas through enmity and strife it will be degraded and its inhabitants scattered.

order.why: Let a shared feast suggest the pleasure of learning together.
Read differences as a reason for stronger connection.
shortened: The Blessed Beauty addresses humanity saying "Ye are all fruits of one tree," meaning you are all fruits and leaves of the tree of existence. Therefore although there are differences among you, these differences should not be the cause of conflict and strife, rather they should lead to the utmost connection and harmony with one another.

order.why: Hear the tree image addressed to religions and peoples.
shortened: Baha'u'llah addresses all peoples, religions and faiths [saying]: "Ye are all the fruits of one tree, and the leaves of one branch."

order.why: Recall that image amid mutual reviling.
Keep the reported repetition of the same appeal.
Retain the concise universal address.
Imagine different letters making one word.
shortened: Today the leaves of the Divine Lote-Tree warble in melodies and strains which, were the people of the world to hearken unto even less than these, they would witness all differing things, contrasting forms, and divergent views united as the letters of one blessed word.

order.why: Consider how varied forms adorn one another.
shortened: Since they are under the training of one Gardener, are watered from one water, are nurtured by the heat of one sun, receive bounty from one breeze, and grow from one soil, their different colors, compositions, forms, shapes, tastes and fragrances cause the adornment and splendor of one another.

order.why: Return to the many-colored rose garden.
Let tongues and peoples enrich that garden.
Join varied fruit with shared nourishment.
See each tree’s beauty increased by its neighbors.
Let children hear of distant flowers’ growth.
shortened: Evidently the rose garden of the West is most beautiful. Its flowers blossomed delightfully. The fragrance there- of is reaching even this remote district, and may this cause the rose garden of the East to be proud of this, that, praise be to God, the rose garden of the West, in a short space of time, has assumed most delightful freshness.

White flowers have grown in it; colored flowers have grown in it; red flowers can be seen in it; and yellow flowers can be seen in it, and all of these together are in the utmost of freshness and verdure, and each lends a charm and harmony to the others. Each one is a cause of adornment to the others.

order.why: Consider different conditions in which fruits ripen.
shortened: Paris is the universal center of culture and learning, of science and the arts. She must also be the center of spirituality. There are all sorts of fruits; some can only ripen in a cold climate; others need the warmth and others yet the tropical sun. So it is with Paris.

order.why: Read shared growth through the Kingdom’s garden.
Keep distinct waves within the unending sea.
shortened: My hope is that all the handmaids of God in that region will unite like unto the waves of one unending sea; for although blown about as the wind listeth, these are separate in themselves, yet in truth are they all at one with the boundless deep.

order.why: Join one light and many lamps with mutual love.
shortened: The maid-servants of the Merciful should love each other with heart and soul; for though there be many bodies, the spirit of faith is one and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit is universal. There is one Light but many lamps; there is one Wine but the glasses differ.

order.why: Let different bodies share illumination.
Read many persons through one spiritual orientation.
Keep covenant, sea, sky and common service together.
shortened: The believers of God are the waves of one Sea, the drops of one River, the signs of one Kingdom, the standards of one Regiment, the lights of one Orb, the Armies of one General, the stars of one Heaven and are addressed by one Covenant.

order.why: Explore spiritual love as a bond among peoples.
Consider the strength of acting in unison.
shortened: Whensoever holy souls, drawing on the powers of heaven, shall arise with such qualities of the spirit, and march in unison, rank on rank, every one of those souls will be even as one thousand, and the surging waves of that mighty ocean will be even as the battalions of the Concourse on high.

order.why: Attend to the invitation to hear a shared spiritual melody.
Preserve the source’s question mark in its account of spiritual fellowship.
Keep astonishment at strangers’ affection and familiar people’s estrangement.
Pray for prejudice to give way to concord.
shortened: Turn these souls into heavenly angels, resuscitate them through the breath of Thy Holy Spirit, grant them eloquent tongues and resolute hearts, bestow on them heavenly power and merciful susceptibilities, cause them to become the promulgators of the oneness of mankind and the cause of love and concord in the world of humanity, so that the perilous darkness of ignorant prejudice may vanish through the light of the Sun of Truth, this dreary world may become illumined, this material realm may absorb the rays of the world of spirit, these different colors may merge into one color and the melody of praise may rise to the kingdom of Thy sanctity.

order.why: Gather varied images beneath one bounty.
shortened: Unite all beneath the shade of Your bounty and make all in agreement, so that all may become rays of one sun, waves of one sea, fruits of one tree, drink from one fountain, be stirred by one breeze, and derive light from one source.

order.why: Pray for descendants of Israel and Ishmael to share an assembly.
Imagine a tent where opposing peoples find rest.
Pray for continuing spiritual fellowship.
Join unity with mutual support and sacrifice.
Let love gather multiplicities.
Give thanks for united hearts.
Gather the scattered flock beneath a shared Shepherd.
Pray through many images of essential oneness.
shortened: Those who believe in God and are confident in His Word shall enter the Kingdom, and the essential oneness appears among them to such an extent that all become the drops of one ocean, the rays of one sun, the fishes of one sea, the trees of one garden, the birds of one orchard, the candles of one assembly and the stars of the same heaven.

order.why: Remember the labor behind the invitation to one table.
Bring scattered birds and thirsty souls into companionship.
shortened: We beseech God that He may gather all through pure grace beneath the canopy of His gift, and unite all at the spring of Tasnim; that He may make these scattered birds in the wilderness of separation intimate companions in the meadow of reality, and cause these gazelles of the plain of oneness to roam together in the garden of spirituality; that He may bring the yearning ones into the bridal chamber of reunion and give the thirsty ones to drink from the eternal spring of life.

order.why: Pray for healing of scattered hearts.
shortened: O Pure One of God, heal the scattered hearts and unite the thoughts of the helpless ones. Be a kind shepherd to the dispersed flock and a blessed gatherer of scattered birds. Illumine the hearts with the light of unity and make souls alive and stirred by the breaths of fellowship.

order.why: Close the linked readings with love stirring life to motion.
shortened: Such passion and fervor of love, such tumult of attraction, such jubilation of melody and song, that the atoms of all things begin to dance with delight and the reality of beings becomes stirred into motion.

order.why: Retain the supplied dove and eye imagery.
Return to the supplied garden’s distinct charms.
Consider the preservation of inherited cultural identity.
Read cultural traditions within the stated ethical boundary.
Bring diversity into assemblies and shared administration.
Widen the inquiry to a diverse world society.
shortened: Acceptance of the oneness of mankind is the first fundamental prerequisite for reorganization and administration of the world as one country, the home of humankind.

In the Baha'i view, recognition of the oneness of mankind "calls for no less than the reconstruction and the demilitarization of the whole civilized world -- a world organically unified in all the essential aspects of its life, its political machinery, its spiritual aspiration, its trade and finance, its script and language, and yet infinite in the diversity of the national characteristics of its federated units."

order.why: Examine identity through shared purpose and humanity’s interests.
shortened: Consider how radically different such a fragmented conception of human identity is from the one that follows from a recognition of the oneness of humanity. In this perspective, the diversity that characterizes the human family, far from contradicting its oneness, endows it with richness. Unity, in its Baha'i expression, contains the essential concept of diversity, distinguishing it from uniformity. It is through love for all people, and by subordinating lesser loyalties to the best interests of humankind, that the unity of the world can be realized and the infinite expressions of human diversity find their highest fulfilment.

order.why: Close with complementary action and the truth that no person can do everything.
shortened: A unity in diversity of actions is called for, a condition in which different individuals will concentrate on different activities, appreciating the salutary effect of the aggregate on the growth and development of the Faith, because each person cannot do everything and all persons cannot do the same thing.

questions: How do the body, garden, ocean, and musical chord reveal different aspects of unity, and where might each image leave questions unanswered?
How can a community distinguish differences that enrich its life from antagonisms that injure it without suppressing individuality?
What habits of teaching, listening, consultation, and practical care help people with different understandings contribute to a shared purpose?
What would equal regard across race and culture require beyond sharing a room, a name, or an institution?
How do Paul’s account of necessary members and the Qur’an’s invitation to know one another deepen this inquiry, while retaining their distinct religious settings?
How might a community preserve cultural identities and welcome different kinds of service while remaining accountable to common principles and the well-being of the whole?

references.label: 1 · 1 Corinthians 12:12–27 · Many necessary members
references.note: Paul describes the Christian community as the body of Christ, insisting that different members need one another and that those thought weaker are necessary. Shared suffering and rejoicing make the image practical. Compare this account with the compilation’s bodily metaphors, attending both to mutual care and to the different scope of each use of the image.

references.label: 2 · Qur’an 49:13 · Peoples and mutual knowledge
references.note: This verse addresses humanity through common creation, distinct peoples and tribes, and the purpose of knowing one another. It relates honor before God to righteousness or piety rather than ancestry. Compare that account with the compilation’s treatment of race, cultural difference, and good character; the parallel translations also invite attention to how its key terms are expressed.
